items.text: Nvidia said Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, after reports of affairs including one with a woman US intelligence reportedly suspected of spying for China. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO (staying CFO), Harvey C. Jones becomes the company's first board chair, and the board is searching internal and external candidates. Nvidia says it will still report earnings on Nov 17.
items.notes: Closes W-261112-01. Company announcement (8-K link seen in search, not opened). CBS (Alex Sundby) also confirms.

items.text: Huang has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, House Foreign Affairs chair Brian Mast said. The Foreign Affairs, China Select and Intelligence committee chairs had requested his appearance on Nov 4, and several lawmakers had threatened a subpoena.
items.notes: No hearing date set.

items.text: US stocks fell about 0.4% across the S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq after Huang's exit; Nvidia closed down 4.3% after falling as much as 14% early (Investopedia). The 10-year Treasury yield rose back above 5%, reaching above 5.10%, after weak demand at a $25bn 30-year bond auction, and WTI rose about 2.8% to near $89 after Trump said the US doesn't need an Iran deal. Markets now fully price a December Fed hike (TipRanks).
items.notes: Auction bid-to-cover: TokenPost 2.401; TheStreet 2.36 with 5.441% high yield. Exact closing yield not confirmed.

items.text: Several Fed officials leaned toward more tightening: Philadelphia's Anna Paulson said further gradual tightening seems appropriate, Chicago's Goolsbee said inflation looks to be going the wrong way, and Cleveland's Hammack favoured smaller, more frequent increases. Initial jobless claims were 200,000 for the week ending Nov 7.
items.notes: Some remarks (e.g. Bowman) were from earlier in the week. October PPI was due Nov 13 at 8:30 ET; not yet seen.

items.text: AP called Mississippi's Senate race for Democrat Scott Colom on the evening of Nov 11, when he led Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 4,669 votes of about 962,000 counted (roughly 0.5 points), with fewer than 12,000 votes left to review. Hyde-Smith conceded in a video, saying she respects voters' decision. Colom is the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Mississippi since 1982, which gives Democrats 55 seats with Alaska still uncalled.
items.notes: Closes W-261106-02. Deseret says 'first Democratic senator since 1947', which conflicts with Fox8/Gray ('first elected since 1982'); used 1982. County certification due Nov 13.

items.text: Trump posted on Truth Social that the US no longer needs a deal with Iran, saying it controls Iran's money and the Strait of Hormuz, and told VP Vance, who had led the talks, to focus on corruption and crime in Democratic-run states and cities. Trump later told Hugh Hewitt he could resume strikes, possibly right away, while having told 60 Minutes he is not looking to escalate.
items.notes: Trump's own post; NBC, Axios and SCMP also reported it.

items.text: Iranian officials said Washington must accept seven conditions before any talks. Security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Hormuz stays closed until they are met and the nuclear issue is off the table, and Speaker Ghalibaf said they must be fully implemented first. Tehran has not published the list; the only one named is an end to the war on all fronts, especially Lebanon.
items.notes: Iran International is an opposition-leaning outlet; Al Jazeera link (Nov 11) is consistent on Hormuz staying shut.

items.text: Anthropic's IPO is about six times oversubscribed, Bloomberg reported (via Reuters). The company set a $70–78 range on Nov 10 for 825 million shares, raising up to about $64.4bn at a valuation of up to $1.4tn, with Nasdaq trading under ticker ANT expected around Nov 19.
items.notes: Closes W-261027-01 (the range and roadshow were launched Nov 10). Oversubscription comes from Bloomberg sources.

items.text: Digital Affairs Minister Gawkowski said the ePUAP cyberattack came from abroad and was part of a longer plan to paralyse public administration during the December peak, with the intruders preparing what he called an 'administrative bomb'. He has not named the country of origin, and says he will do so once experts confirm it. ePUAP was still offline on Thursday with no restoration date; the ABW and NASK are investigating. Gawkowski said citizens are not at risk.
items.notes: Updates W-261112-03 (still pending: no restoration yet). Interia (Martyna Piotrowska) adds Gawkowski's remark about a 'digital war with Russia', but Russia was not formally named as the attacker.

items.text: President Nawrocki has until Friday Nov 13 to sign, veto or refer to the Tribunal the second DSA-implementing law, which creates a fast procedure for orders blocking illegal online content (with court approval except for categories such as child sexual abuse material). Gawkowski presented a report on young victims of online platforms and urged a signature; presidential spokesman Leśkiewicz warned against executive blocking without court involvement. Poland is the last EU state without DSA rules.
items.notes: Decision NOT confirmed at research time (search budget ran out). Nawrocki vetoed the earlier version in January 2026.

items.text: Suspended Constitutional Tribunal president Święczkowski went to the Tribunal with judges Sochański, Piotrowicz and Wyrembak. He showed police a Nov 10 Supreme Court ruling that lifted his and Sochański's suspension, but officers refused them entry. He hung the ruling on the fence, threatened to call a bailiff and announced further attempts next week. Acting head Judge Korwin-Piotrowska says the SN ruling does not affect the suspension.
items.notes: The Nov 10 SN ruling (judges Szczepaniec and Dobrowolski) was not in earlier briefs. Rzeczpospolita (Ada Michalak) adds the fence and bailiff details.

items.text: Justice Minister Żurek dismissed the Supreme Court ruling for Święczkowski, saying it was issued by judges appointed on the neo-KRS's recommendation. In his view, SN judge Korzeniowski's Nov 6 decision (that the chamber had no jurisdiction and the Tribunal is the proper forum) stands. He mocked the idea of enforcing the ruling with a 'potato stamp'.
items.notes: Contested: the right-wing press (wPolityce headline: police 'scared of a piece of paper') presents the SN ruling as binding. The wPolityce article could not be fetched.

items.text: Police delivered an order from Szczecin district prosecutors to TV Republika demanding recordings, logs and staff rosters from the Oct 16 events outside the Constitutional Tribunal. The investigation covers calls to reveal a policewoman's identity, insults to officers and the PM, and threats against police. Prosecutors say no devices or journalistic sources were sought; Justice Minister Żurek defended the move. PiS leader Kaczyński called it a 'storm on independent media', and wPolsce24 refuses a similar request from Warsaw prosecutors.
items.notes: Editor-in-chief Sakiewicz called it a scandal (per lublin112 and naszapolska headlines). The case was moved from Warsaw to Szczecin over impartiality concerns.

items.text: Gdańsk-Śródmieście district prosecutors have asked to question President Nawrocki as a witness in the investigation into how he acquired the studio flat of Jerzy Ż. (suspected fraud against the elderly man, 2012–2017). The letter went to the Chancellery on Nov 9, and the date is left to the President. The regional prosecutors' spokesman confirmed it to PAP.
items.notes: No Chancellery reaction found. A niezalezna.pl headline attacks Onet's source as a convicted fraudster (headline only).

items.text: The EU Court of Justice dismissed all seven complaints Poland filed in 2023 against Fit for 55 climate acts, including emissions trading, car CO2 standards and energy efficiency. The court held that qualified-majority voting was lawful, not unanimity, and rejected Poland's arguments on energy solidarity and social costs, pointing to compensation such as the Social Climate Fund.
items.notes: No government reaction found in the sources read. Right-wing outlets (Fronda, Do Rzeczy) blame Tusk, although the complaints were filed by the Morawiecki government.

items.text: At the European Political Community summit in Dublin, PM Tusk met President Zelensky. They discussed winter support for Ukraine, fuel deliveries from Poland and transport links, Ukraine's EU accession, and training for the 'coalition of the willing', whose first stage takes place in Poland.
items.notes: Mostly based on Zelensky's post on X.

items.text: Maximum fuel prices for Friday Nov 13: petrol 95 at 6.06 zł/l, petrol 98 at 6.68 zł/l and diesel at 7.54 zł/l, all down from Thursday (diesel by 12 gr). The next notice will cover Saturday to Monday.

MPC member Iwona Duda said policy may need tightening to prevent lasting excess inflation and that rate cuts are off the table for now; ING calls the Council's tone hawkish and expects a hike in early 2027. Deputy Finance Minister Neneman said LPG will not be added to the fuel price caps. Retail bond sales were 8.2bn zł in October.
items.notes: Bank research digest dated Nov 12; Duda's remarks probably date from Nov 11. EUR/PLN was 4.415 on Nov 11.

items.text: GIS warned against drinking one batch of Jurajska Sport still mineral water (700 ml, best before 29.07.2027) after mould and contaminants were found, and the producer is withdrawing it. GIS also extended its warning on BRAIN WASH hemp gummies and a shot from Kalisz-based DR JOINT to further batches over possible THC content.
items.notes: The BRAIN WASH update was issued by GIS on Nov 10.

items.text: The ABW said it detained two Ukrainian citizens in Mińsk Mazowiecki on Nov 3, suspected of spying and sabotage for Russian intelligence. They allegedly scouted military and critical infrastructure and burned vehicles fitted with plates resembling Ukrainian army ones, and were paid partly in cryptocurrency. A court remanded both for three months; they face 10 years to life.
items.notes: Announced Nov 10 but missed in earlier briefs.

items.text: Małopolska voivode Krzysztof Klęczar said on Thursday that 11 people injured in the attack remain in five Kraków hospitals and their condition is steadily improving. A 27-year-old woman with serious liver injuries was moved to the Central Clinical Hospital in Warsaw and an Austrian man to Vienna. One wounded officer was moved to the Military Hospital in Kraków for hand reconstruction surgery; the other is stable at the John Paul II hospital.
items.notes: WP also reports, citing the carriage drivers' association, that a carriage driver shot four times is conscious but in very serious condition, with a spinal injury. Klęczar says the government will help victims' families but no formal aid requests have been filed yet (Interia).

items.text: Eryk Stasielak, head of the Kraków branch of the National Prosecutor's Office, told Fakt that no decision has been made on burying the attacker, whose body cannot stay at the forensic institute indefinitely, and did not rule out that the state could arrange it. A relative has offered to bury the attacker's parents and sister.
items.notes: No new findings on motive or accomplices found for 12-13 Nov; W-261110-02 remains open.

items.text: City Hall has written to some municipal units asking for large savings from January 2027, according to a trade-union representative quoted by KRKnews. Options under discussion include freezing pay at 2026 levels and cutting bonuses, and the annual December award (about 2,500–3,000 zł per employee) is uncertain in some units.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Comes ahead of the 2027 budget draft due 15 Nov (W-261026-18). Article repeats the ~390m zł current-spending gap and projected debt of ~8.98bn zł at end-2026.

items.text: Police detained a man near ul. Bieżanowska after he fired at officers who were responding to a report of a man with a weapon. Officers fired warning shots and no one was hurt. Police later said the gun was a CO2-powered air revolver.
items.notes: Radio Kraków/PAP first said it looked like a blank-firing gun; CoWKrakowie's update cites police saying CO2 pneumatic revolver, and gives his age as 39.

items.text: A car went off the al. 29 Listopada viaduct, knocking down four street lamps, and fell onto ul. Wita Stwosza. Firefighters cut out the driver, a man of about 70, who was taken to hospital with a broken arm and head injury. Wita Stwosza has reopened.

The agenda for the City Council's 64th session on 18 November (11:00) is published. It includes the second readings of the mayor's draft suspending the partnership with Lviv (druk 1586) and the fare resolution (druk 1587, with a Nowa Lewica amendment and a mayoral self-amendment), a mayoral statement on freezing Clean Transport Zone fees, honours for medics who helped on 7 November, and first readings of 2027 property and vehicle tax rates.
items.thread: Kraków–Lviv partnership and the Year of the UPA
items.notes: Publication date of agenda not shown; seen 13 Nov. Not on the agenda: honorary citizenship for the two officers, the Music Centre resolution (W-261106-11), the 2027 budget, Eurocities exit.

items.text: IMGW issued a level-1 warning for heavy snow in Tatra and Nowy Targ counties, with 5–10 cm of new snow above 500 m forecast for 04:00–12:00 on 13 November. IMGW also flagged yellow snow warnings for southern Małopolska, with 20–35 mm of precipitation overnight in the south of the region.
items.notes: Kraków itself was not listed in the warnings seen.

items.text: Kraków will hold a free memorial organ concert for the victims of the 7 November attack at St Mary's Basilica on Saturday evening, 14 November, with Hungarian organist Xaver Varnus playing Bach and improvisations.

The Kraków Merchants' Congregation published an appeal asking residents to keep coming to the city centre's shops and restaurants after the attack, saying fear must not close the city. It invited people to the upcoming Christmas Market on the Main Square.
items.notes: No figures on business losses given.

items.text: Sebastian Lipowski, until now head of the City Hall department for social policy, equality and health, became director of the Municipal Addiction Prevention Centre on 10 November, replacing Rafał Kręgulec. Przemysław Cichy has taken over the department's duties.
